task_instance: Write a small C++ target (parse_buffer) with an intentional heap-buffer-overflow bug, write an LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harness for it, compile with clang++ -fsanitize=fuzzer,address, run a libFuzzer campaign against a seed corpus, confirm it finds and saves a crashing input, and reproduce the crash from the saved artifact.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/trailofbits__skills__libfuzzer . Files: target.cc (parse_buffer() with unchecked memcpy(buf, data+1, len) into an 8-byte malloc'd buffer), harness.cc (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput calling parse_buffer). Build: `clang++ -fsanitize=fuzzer,address -g -O0 harness.cc target.cc -o fuzz` succeeded (exit 0), producing executable `fuzz`. Corpus seeded with 2 files in corpus/. Ran `./fuzz -max_len=64 corpus/` (via run.log); within the first few executions (#5 INITED) it found: 'ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 4 ... in parse_buffer(unsigned char const*, unsigned long) target.cc:15:5, called from LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harness.cc:8:5', and libFuzzer wrote the crashing input to ./crash-769af93e7ee3d67675c531de9537eb764d660344 (2 bytes: 0x04 0x04). Verified reproducibility by re-running `./fuzz crash-769af93e7ee3d67675c531de9537eb764d660344`, which again produced 'SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... in __asan_memcpy' with the same stack trace, confirming a deterministic, reproducible crash. This exercises the skill's full core deliverable: harness authoring, -fsanitize=fuzzer/address build, corpus setup, campaign execution, crash discovery/triage, and reproduction — all achievable directly in this runtime with the preinstalled clang/LLVM toolchain (no missing tools, credentials, or network access were needed).
